title: WordPress Core unauthenticated RCE race during core upgrades (CVE-2026-119977) now in CISA KEV
action: Confirm every WordPress site is on 7.1.4 (or its branch backport), deny web access to wp-content/upgrade/ at the web server, and hunt logs for requests to PHP files under wp-content/upgrade.
product: WordPress Core 4.7 through 7.1.3 (fixed in 7.1.4 and backported branch releases)

title: Synology DSM NAS hit by C3RB3R (Cerber) ransomware via unauthenticated DSM flaws; Synology confirms exploitation, not in CISA KEV
why: Synology's Oct 29 notice confirms threat actors are exploiting a vulnerability patched in December 2024 (it points to SA-24:20, CVE-2024-10441) to encrypt outdated DSM devices. Qihoo 360's Oct 29 incident analysis attributes the cases it examined to unauthenticated CVE-2026-13639/13684 (SA-26:13, Sep 18) instead, so which flaw is used is disputed. BleepingComputer (Nov 2) reports a wave of victims; Shadowserver tracks 380k+ exposed Synology NAS. Missing on Microsoft's side: none of the three CVEs appears in CISA KEV (collector KEV feed shows no Synology additions; pentest-tools lists CVE-2024-10441 as not in KEV, undated). Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Nov 4: collector's CISA KEV feed added only WordPress CVE-2026-119977, and Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 3) does not include this one, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Update every Synology NAS to the latest DSM build for its branch (at least 7.4-90075 / 7.3.2-86009-4 / 7.2.2-72806-9 / 7.2.1-69057-12), take DSM management ports off the internet, and search shares for .L0CK3D files and read-me3.txt.

title: APT29 'Poisoned Source' watering holes and Plerdy supply-chain hijack deliver n-day iOS/Android exploit chains (DarkSword)
why: Not ahead: every CVE in the chains is an n-day that was patched before the campaign (Sekoia). DarkSword's CVE-2025-43529 has been used by several groups since Nov 2025. The actor is Midnight Blizzard, which Microsoft tracks. KEV status of each CVE was not re-checked this run.
action: Enforce current iOS and Chrome versions on managed phones through MDM, and review third-party analytics scripts on your sites. Plerdy customers should check the Aug 27-Sep 3 window.
product: iOS 16.7 and 18.5 (Safari/WebKit chains); Android Chrome 139-145 with Adreno GPU

title: Supermarket refrigeration-controller sabotage spreads to Belgium and Sweden: Delhaize, Carrefour Belgium and ICA fridges driven to 50°C overnight Nov 1-2
why: New wave: NL Times (Nov 2) reports at least dozens of Delhaize stores, butcher De Laet & Van Haver and 15 Carrefour Belgium stores hit late Nov 1/early Nov 2, and Swedish media report ICA stores with cooling at 50°C overnight (HN discussion, Sweden Herald). Same pattern as the Oct 11-12 French campaign (CERT-FR CERTFR-2026-ALE-012: numerous compromised Danfoss AK-SM/AK-SC controllers). A public PoC for the Danfoss 'code of the day' auth bypass CVE-2025-41450 has been on GitHub since Oct 13. CISA's KEV file listed no Danfoss entry as of Oct 12 and none appear in KEV additions Oct 25-31; no authority has confirmed which flaw is used (the CVE link is inference). Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Nov 4: collector's CISA KEV feed added only WordPress CVE-2026-119977, and Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 3) does not include this one, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Take every refrigeration/building controller off the public internet now (contractor access only via VPN with MFA), upgrade AK-SM 8xxA to R4.3.1+, plan replacement of EOL AK-SM 800/AK-SC 355, and check setpoints and defrost schedules against baseline.
product: Danfoss AK-SM 800A / AK-SM 8xxA System Manager before R4.3.1 (auth bypass fixed in R4.2), end-of-life AK-SM 800 and AK-SC 355; Copeland/Dixell XWEB controllers

title: CryptoPayment Gateway WordPress plugin: unpatched unauthenticated admin-action flaw (CVSS 10.0) exposing wallet credentials now under exploitation attempts
why: Defused Cyber reported in-the-wild exploitation attempts (starting Nov 2) from 'KYC-free VPS' infrastructure; The Hacker News covered it Nov 3. WPScan says no fix exists. Not in CISA KEV (OpenCVE; collector KEV feed shows no additions). Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Nov 4: collector's CISA KEV feed added only WordPress CVE-2026-119977, and Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 3) does not include this one, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Remove the CryptoPayment Gateway plugin from any WordPress site, rotate the wallet keys it stored, and audit for deleted files or changed gateway settings.
product: CryptoPayment Gateway WordPress plugin 1.2.1 through 1.2.2 (no fix; plugin closed on WordPress.org since Aug 28, 2026)

title: InternLM LMDeploy unauthenticated RCE via pickle in /update_weights (CVSS 9.3), reproduction code public
why: VulnCheck CVE published Oct 30; GitHub issue #4698 contains reproduction code showing request-controlled pickle deserialization. No fixed release is named in the sources and no ITW reports; not in CISA KEV. Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Nov 4: collector's CISA KEV feed added only WordPress CVE-2026-119977, and Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 3) does not include this one, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Take LMDeploy api_server off untrusted networks (bind to localhost or front with auth and --api-keys) and block /update_weights until a fixed release is confirmed.

title: Android 'SMS of Death': now listed in Google's November 2026 bulletin; public zero-click PoC, Android 12/13 still without a fix
why: A working public PoC (Mark Blaszczyk, Oct 29) crashes com.android.phone with one 8-byte WAP Push SMS and can boot-loop devices. Change Nov 3: the CVE record now references Google's November 2026 Android Security Bulletin (fix shipped in October updates for Android 14-17); reports still say Android 12/13 get no fix. No in-the-wild attacks reported; not in CISA KEV. Rechecked Nov 4: collector's CISA KEV feed added only WordPress CVE-2026-119977, and Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 3) does not include this one, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Use MDM to require Android security patch level 2026-11-01 or later on managed phones and retire or restrict Android 12/13 devices that will not be patched.
product: Android telephony framework (WapPushOverSms/decodeWapPdu), Android 12 through 16; fixed in October 2026 updates for Android 14-17 only

title: Northflank PaaS breach: customers told to assume all environment variables decrypted; stolen AI API keys already abused
why: Northflank's status page (Oct 30-31) confirms multiple customers saw unauthorized use of AI API keys stored on the platform and tells all customers to assume every environment variable was decrypted; Wiz raised the alert and lists Northflank among nine AI-developer-platform incidents in October (LLMJacking). Entry point and customer count undisclosed. A SaaS breach, so no KEV/MSRC entry applies. Rechecked Nov 4: collector's CISA KEV feed added only WordPress CVE-2026-119977, and Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 3) does not include this one, so it is still not in KEV.
action: If you use Northflank, revoke and reissue every secret stored there at the issuing provider (AI, cloud, database), disable public add-on access, and review AI-provider usage and billing logs since Oct 30.
product: Northflank cloud application platform (customer environment variables, secret groups, global secrets)

title: Chainstack production breach (customer data, password hashes, node credentials) tied to ARTEX AI-agent intrusion campaign also hitting WorkOS and Chainalysis
why: Chainstack disclosed on Nov 3 that an attacker entered through a third-party component on Oct 26, reached production and a database of customer names, emails and password hashes, and could access systems holding node credentials (The Hacker News, Mallory). The Hacker News links it to the ARTEX autonomous-agent campaign (China-linked cluster) that also breached WorkOS and Chainalysis; that attribution is an assessment, not confirmed by Chainstack. No CVE, so nothing in CISA KEV; no Microsoft report on ARTEX seen.
action: If you use Chainstack, change account passwords, rotate all node credentials and regenerate platform API keys now, and review node/API usage since Oct 26.
product: Chainstack blockchain node platform (console accounts, node credentials, platform API keys)

title: Rails Active Storage ImageMagick unauthenticated arbitrary file write/read (CVE-2026-122006, CVSS 9.8)
why: On Nov 4 Rails published GHSA-f3w6-w445-fwh9, now CVE-2026-122006: an uploaded crafted file can write arbitrary files and, with the Disk service, read secret_key_base. THN and Ostorlab covered it. No public exploit and not in CISA KEV (HOL Guard, Nov 4). Not a Microsoft product.
action: Upgrade to Rails 8.1.4.1 or 8.0.5.2 (with mini_magick 5.1 or later). Confirm the shipped ImageMagick policy loads, and move 7.2 or older apps to a supported series.
product: activestorage before 8.0.5.2 and 8.1.x before 8.1.4.1 (apps using ImageMagick/mini_magick)

title: Android Framework zero-click RCE (CVE-2026-58868) in November 2026 bulletin, Android 14-17
why: Google rates CVE-2026-58868 Critical: a heap overflow in FrameDecoder.cpp that allows remote code execution with no user interaction (November bulletin, THN, Security Affairs, Rescana). It is not in CISA KEV (Nov 3 catalog). Not a Microsoft product.
action: Use MDM to flag Android devices below security patch level 2026-11-01 (2026-11-05 covers the whole bulletin), and set a deadline to update or replace them.

title: Sogou Input Method for Windows exploited in the wild: SlippyNunchucks hijacks HTTP config to deploy DarkVigil
why: ESET reports a China-aligned group (SlippyNunchucks) has exploited SGTool.exe's plain-HTTP config retrieval since July 1, 2026. It redirects DNS for the Sogou config host and delivers the DarkVigil/FDMTP implant to victims in six countries (THN, Infosecurity, NVD Nov 4). Not in CISA KEV (TheHackerWire). Not a Microsoft product, so no MSRC advisory applies.
action: Inventory Windows endpoints running Sogou Input Method and update them to 16.10 or later, or remove it. Hunt for unexpected DLLs written by SGTool.exe.
product: Sogou Input Method for Windows before 16.10

title: Barracuda Email Security Gateway pre-auth config-restore bypass (CVSS4 9.3) chains with root command injection CVE-2026-111560; fixed 9.4.0.030
why: Barracuda and Mandiant (MNDT-2026-0042/0041) disclosed on Nov 2 that an unauthenticated attacker who can reach the ESG admin interface (port 8000 by default) can restore a crafted config backup, and chained with the timezone command injection gets root. No exploitation or public PoC reported. Missing on Microsoft's side: neither CVE is in CISA KEV (HOL: not on KEV as of catalog 2026.10.30, and none of Barracuda, Mandiant or CISA reports exploitation). Barracuda ESG was mass-exploited in 2023, so it is a likely target. Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Nov 4: collector's CISA KEV feed added only WordPress CVE-2026-119977, and Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 3) does not include this one, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade ESG to 9.4.0.030 or later (patch BNSF-40425/40430), set Firmware Patches to apply automatically, and make sure the admin interface (port 8000) is not reachable from the internet.
product: Barracuda Email Security Gateway before 9.4.0.030 (CVE-2026-116606); CVE-2026-111560 also hits Load Balancer ADC <=6.4.0, WAF <=11.0.1, Web Security Gateway <=16.1.100.100, Message Archiver <=5.5.4.0, WAF Control Center <=2.2.1

title: ManageEngine Log360 / EventLog Analyzer unauthenticated unauthorized-access flaw (CVSS 9.1) fixed after build 13062
why: Zoho published the CVE and fix on Nov 3 (CVSS 9.1, AV:N/PR:N); details are withheld. No PoC or exploitation reported and not in CISA KEV (TheHackerWire; collector KEV feed). ManageEngine products have a history of KEV-listed auth bypasses. Not a Microsoft product. Rechecked Nov 4: collector's CISA KEV feed added only WordPress CVE-2026-119977, and Senserva's KEV-last-7-days list (updated Nov 3) does not include this one, so it is still not in KEV.
action: Upgrade Log360 and EventLog Analyzer to the build after 13062 named in Zoho's advisory and restrict the web console to admin networks.
product: ManageEngine Log360 and EventLog Analyzer builds 13062 and below

title: Cisco ISE / ISE-PIC unauthenticated authorization bypass lets attackers obtain an endpoint identity certificate
why: Cisco PSIRT published this on Nov 4: an unauthenticated remote attacker can obtain an endpoint identity certificate from ISE with a crafted request. No exploitation or PoC reported, and not in CISA KEV (Senserva KEV-7d, Nov 4).
action: Check the Cisco advisory for fixed ISE releases and patch. Restrict access to ISE interfaces with infrastructure ACLs until then.
product: Cisco Identity Services Engine (ISE) and ISE Passive Identity Connector

title: Xen XSA-523 grant-copy flaws let a malicious guest read/write any domain's memory including dom0
why: Xen published XSA-523 on Nov 3 (found by Anthropic with Claude, validated by Ada Logics): any guest can read and write other domains' memory, including dom0, with no known mitigation. XCP-ng and Qubes shipped fixes, but Debian bookworm/trixie were still vulnerable on Nov 4. No exploitation reported and not in CISA KEV.
action: Apply the XSA-523 patches or your vendor's Xen update (XCP-ng xen-4.17.7-4.2.xcpng8.3, Qubes 4.19.6-3) and reboot hosts that run untrusted guests.
product: Xen 4.6 and later (patches for 4.17-4.19 and unstable); XCP-ng, Qubes OS

title: FreeRDP 3.32.2 fixes 15 memory-safety flaws (CVSS up to 9.3): proxy OOB write, client UAFs, RD Gateway overflow
why: NVD published 15 FreeRDP CVEs on Nov 4, fixed in 3.32.2. They include an out-of-bounds write in freerdp-proxy reachable by any connecting client (9.3) and client use-after-frees triggered by malicious RDP servers (9.3). No PoC or exploitation reported, and not in CISA KEV.
action: Update FreeRDP to 3.32.2 (and distro packages that bundle it), and prioritise any internet-reachable freerdp-proxy or shadow server.

title: Debian/Ubuntu APT man-in-the-middle package swap after verification gives root code execution (DSA-6607-1)
why: Debian DSA-6607-1 (Nov 4, found by Max Justicz): an on-path attacker, such as a malicious mirror or proxy, can swap a package after APT verifies it and get code execution as root. Covered by HN, Phoronix and Mallory. No public PoC or exploitation, and not in CISA KEV.
action: Update apt (3.0.4 trixie / 2.6.2 bookworm / Ubuntu USN), and use HTTPS mirrors; avoid apt over untrusted networks until patched.
product: APT on Debian 12/13, Ubuntu 22.04+ and derivatives (Acquire::Retries non-zero, default since bookworm/jammy)

title: SonicWall GMS 9.5.2 and earlier: unauthenticated internal file read (CVSS 9.1), plus post-auth SQLi CVE-2026-109594
why: SonicWall advisory SNWLID-2026-0019 (Nov 3) discloses an unauthenticated file read in GMS; SecurityOnline and VulDB cover it. VulDB says no technical details or exploit are public (a Sploitus listing only repeats the description). Not in CISA KEV. SonicWall management products are frequent targets.
action: Update GMS to 9.5.3 or migrate to NSM, and make sure the GMS web interface is not reachable from the internet.
product: SonicWall Global Management System (GMS) 9.5.2 and earlier (fixed 9.5.3 per PT Security; GMS is end-of-life, SonicWall recommends NSM)
